title: Mixtape and Playlist
premise: Casper Galloway, the only out kid in the fading town of Bellhaven, has survived three years by keeping her head down — until her best friend Juniper vanishes, leaving behind a ring of keys and a half-finished mixtape. The keys open every door in the town's shuttered music hall, home of the Founders' Audition, a century-old tradition that made Bellhaven famous and now keeps it from dying. Following Juniper's trail through locked rooms, old recordings, and her grandmother's hidden past, Casper discovers the audition was quietly cancelled by the town council to sell the hall — and that Juniper disappeared trying to stop it. In the end, Casper stages one final audition with the whole town watching, finds Juniper hiding in the hall's attic archive, and claims her own place on its stage, out loud and unafraid.
about_author: Oscar Galloway is the pen name of a former small-town radio DJ who grew up in a community of fewer than a thousand people, where the annual talent show was the only thing that ever filled the gymnasium. They write stories about queer kids finding their voices in places that would rather they stayed quiet.

chapters.title: The Careful Years
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. We meet seventeen-year-old Casper navigating Bellhaven's nine hundred residents, her careful invisibility, and her fierce friendship with Juniper Reyes, who drags her to explore the condemned music hall. Beat: longing disguised as contentment; the reader feels how much Casper has shrunk herself to fit.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Doors
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Juniper shows Casper the keys she's been collecting — old brass keys that fit the music hall's every lock — and plays her a mixtape labeled 'for the last audition.' That night, Juniper doesn't answer her texts. Beat: dread blooming beneath ordinary warmth.

chapters.title: What She Left Behind
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Police search Juniper's house; her parents assume she ran away. Casper finds the keyring abandoned at the hall's stage door and realizes Juniper left them for her deliberately. Beat: guilt ignites into purpose — Casper was chosen, not forgotten.

chapters.title: Every Lock It Fits
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with flashbacks in Juniper's voice from the mixtape. Casper unlocks the hall room by room: practice studios, a projection booth, a wall of century-old audition programs. Each tape track is a map. Beat: wonder braided with grief; the town's buried heart opens under her hands.

chapters.title: The Founders' Audition
chapters.summary: Dual POV via cassette recordings. Casper learns the audition's history — how it built the town, drew crowds for a hundred years — and discovers this year's was secretly cancelled so the council can sell the hall to a developer. Beat: righteous anger; a mystery becomes a mission.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Record
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Digging through family boxes, Casper finds her late grandmother's name in the 1968 program — and a letter revealing Gran was nearly disqualified for singing 'the wrong kind of song,' and hid her queerness her whole life. Beat: inheritance reframed; Casper sees her own fear echoed across generations.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A final tape reveals Juniper discovered councilman Doyle falsified the hall's safety inspection to force the sale — and that he threatened her. The tape cuts off mid-sentence. Beat: terror spikes; the stakes turn personal and dangerous.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper confronts Doyle, gets dismissed as 'a mixed-up kid,' and nearly quits — until townspeople begin quietly offering help: the retired choir teacher, the diner owner, kids she never knew were listening. Beat: the darkest hour before the gathering; isolation breaks.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the night the sale is to be finalized, Casper unlocks the hall, flips the marquee lights on, and holds an open audition. Half the town shows up. Mid-song, she comes out on stage — no careful words, just her name and the truth. Beat: climax; courage as performance and testimony at once.

chapters.title: B-Side
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The council caves; the hall is saved as a landmark. In the attic archive, Casper finds Juniper — hiding, scared, recording everything. Their reconciliation is quiet and real. The book ends with Casper adding her name to next year's program. Beat: belonging earned, memory inherited forward.
